P1.evidence: The best setter read-back in the batch, used twice and with real specificity: 'So I have a brief meeting with Derek. You spoke with him yesterday. So he kind of briefed me in on your situation, like the spine fracture and the fact that you're still fighting with the med board on it. Is that correct?' and again at 00:16:27, 'Derek mentioned to me one thing, that you've waited around a year before reaching out.' The prospect visibly felt known and opened up immediately. But the read-back replaced the open question rather than leading into it — 'what are you potentially looking for help with' was never asked in any form, and the goals emerged only because the prospect volunteered them. No frame, no frame agreement.

P2.evidence: The injury question is the single best moment of diligence in these twelve files: 'With this spine fracture, can you do squats?' It was specific, it was asked early, and it produced exactly the right information — no racked or Smith machine squats because 'it's too easy to overload', but bodyweight squats and physical-therapy-prescribed goblet squats and kettlebell deadlifts are fine. Training frequency, current results and the three-month plateau were all established cleanly, and nutrition was worked meal by meal through to weekends and calorie range. Against that: age, height and weight were all volunteered and never asked, sleep and energy were never raised, and the prospect's actual occupation only emerged at 00:46:45 as a by-product of his work VPN blocking the financing link. Health conditions were inherited from the setter's notes rather than elicited — there was no question about anything beyond the spine, and no hereditary history.

P3.evidence: Complete apart from the edges. The aesthetic goal was separated from the real one cleanly, with the prospect confirming 'it's an aesthetic bonus. I'm already looking the way I want to look.' The bridge was asked explicitly and in the right words: 'if it's only the aesthetics, usually it's okay. But if you want to keep it constant, and for a long run, there has to be something more... that's why I always ask, what's your why behind that?' The who-else question was run properly — 'Holt is your daughter, she's 10, so she's still playing around with you' — and driven through to a concrete image the prospect adopted: 'you don't want to be the dad in Disneyland, sitting on a bench.' The reflect-back landed and the prospect upgraded it himself: rep, 'what you like is the structure. And I think this is what you're lacking right now'; prospect, 'A purpose, really.' Marked short only on P3e, where the rep supplied the answer about health before the prospect could.

P4.evidence: The rep used the setter's note as a lever and it worked: 'Derek mentioned that you've waited around a year before reaching out. So what was actually been holding you back during that time?' That produced the house move, the co-parenting changes, two job changes and the physical therapy. He then refused to settle for it, coming back at 00:19:19 with 'Still, I was missing one piece, like, what's going on? Why have you plateaued for so long?' — which is what surfaced the actual root cause: the gym stopped being fun, 'I really just sat on a machine until my arms got tired.' The prospect named the gap himself in one word, 'purpose', which is the outcome the phase is designed to produce. Only the explicit information-isn't-the-problem framing is absent.

P5.evidence: Two consequence images were used and both were assertions rather than questions — 'if you won't do anything, and you're 35, it's gonna only be downgrading, yeah?' and the Disney bench. The prospect accepted both and even extended one ('I don't want to be hamstringed by not taking care of my body to the point where I can't even go do stuff'), which shows the material was live and would have carried a real question. None was asked. No two-year projection, no willingness to settle, no why-not, no line in the sand. Sixth consecutive call in this batch where this phase does not run, and here it mattered: with no accumulated cost behind the decision, there was nothing to hold the commitment together when the spouse gate appeared.

P6.evidence: The commitment question was asked in near-script form and in the right place, before the price: 'if we can figure out all the logistical details, are you going to be committed to actually showing up and doing the work?' The answer was the strongest yes in the batch — 'Yeah, I'm ready to go. I mean, if we could get me started by next Monday, I would love to start before we leave for the beach.' That is a genuine yes with a self-imposed deadline attached, and the rep correctly moved forward on it. The belief question was not asked, which matters less here than usual because the prospect had been following Trevor for a year and had already done kettlebell work in physical therapy.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and financing was approved live, but the prospect gated on spousal approval and the phase was never reachable. Recorded for completeness: nothing was collected, Trevor's Monday availability was mentioned but no slot was held, no agreement was sent, and no welcome or onboarding instructions were given. The only thing established was the rep's personal WhatsApp as the follow-up channel.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest OB trigger in the batch, arriving with financing already approved and affordability already confirmed — 'I'm not going to drop that money without talking to her about it.' Not one scripted move ran. He did not ask 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal', which the prospect would plainly have answered yes to. He did not ask what obstacles might come up when he talks to her. He did not ask whether there is any reason she would not want him stronger and less in pain — a question with an obvious answer here, since the prospect had just volunteered that his wife is unhappy with her own fitness, asked him to help her get moving, and had been shown Trevor's videos already. He did not ask whether this genuinely needs her input or is permission to bet on himself. He did not offer a deposit with a refund if she said no. Instead he said 'Okay', offered to wait, and spent roughly thirteen minutes on Afghanistan, Poland and Cuban food while the call from her never came. Every ingredient the play needs was on the table and none of it was used.

Trigger was immediate and concrete — 'what does the payment structure for that look like?' followed by 'I just got a mortgage.' The rep did real work: asked about prior third-party financing use, asked the credit score directly and got 580-586, warned it might be tricky, sent the Payva link and secured an approval live at $650 a month over 12 months. That is more of the financial picture than most calls in this batch got. What did not run: no isolation question before the money conversation opened, no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards or available credit, no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. And no company instalment plan was offered as an alternative to third-party financing that adds roughly $1,800 to a $6,000 programme.

notes: Discovery, root cause and goals were run at the highest standard in this batch and produced a prospect who said 'I'm ready to go' with financing approved. It then failed at a single, entirely scripted objection. Coach one thing: when a spouse gate appears, run OB — and here specifically, ask whether there is any reason a wife who has been shown the videos, is unhappy with her own fitness and has asked him to help her get moving would object to him doing this. Second: stop offering to wait. Thirteen minutes of small talk while a callback does not arrive is a call that ends in a follow-up rather than a close.
